title: Did a rare condition cause this 6-car crash?

transcript.text: It's hard to see it first, but the quality is going to get better. A black SUV is driving in the grass just took out a sign. Its turn signal is on, but it's not turning, and now things are going to get interesting fast. One, two, three, four, five, at least five vehicles involved as it bumps the minivan. Rochester, Minnesota, home of the renowned Mayo Clinic, Highway 52, approaching 19th Street is the location, and a number of Minnesotans are going to try to get involved, but the vehicle is going to let out some smoke first, making those individuals reconsider their involvement. The Prius on the right, three or four documents all quickly getting out of the scene. But this is Rochester. Half the town is made up of doctors and nurses, so they're not going to give up quite so easily. I count a crowd of about a dozen with half of them actively assessing, communicating with the patient and each other. Most first responders we've heard from do not recommend getting a patient immediately out of a rollover due to concerns about spinal injuries, unless, of course, something like the car on fire. By coincidence, a tow truck is first on scene, and they're going to start to clear out traffic. They're quickly followed by the medics and fire department, and the cavalry has arrived. But what caused this? State patrol led the investigation and reported that injuries were thankfully minor, and the root cause was a medical issue with the driver. We don't know for certain in this incident, but it may have been caused by a condition called reactive hypoglycemia, which is a subtle. sudden change in your blood pressure, it's more common in those afflicted with diabetes and symptoms include confusion, dizziness, weakness, and loss of consciousness.
